title: UI: Fix tab navigation after closing addon panel
body:
Closes #32583 

## What I did

[Peek 2026-03-03 16-40.webm](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/63f4bff4-ce23-40b5-8e54-8dea70e80c50)

### Testing
#### Manual testing

1. Open Storybook
2. Close addon panel with kb and see where focus lands
3. Open addon panel with kb and see where focus lands
4. Notice that when opening addon panel with kb, we show the region outline because we land on the region for more coherent screen reader announcements

## Copilot slop

Closing the addon panel (via close button or Alt+A shortcut) left focus on the now-removed DOM element, breaking keyboard navigation entirely.

After hiding the panel, focus is now moved to the "Show addon panel" toolbar button, but only when focus was within the panel at the time of closing. If the toolbar button is unavailable, focus falls back to the start of the document. When focus is elsewhere in the app (e.g. sidebar, toolbar, preview), it is left untouched.

- **`layout.ts`**: Added `showAddonPanel` to `focusableUIElements`; added `focusOnUIElement` to `SubAPI` type; refactored `focusOnUIElement` to accept an options object with optional `poll` flag (defaults to `true` for backwards compatibility) and return `boolean | Promise<boolean>` indicating focus success
- **`addons.tsx`**: Added `id="storybook-show-addon-panel"` to the toolbar button
- **`container/Panel.tsx`**: `toggleVisibility` now calls `focusOnUIElement` with `{ poll: false }` when hiding, falling back to `document.body.focus()` on failure; uses `focusableUIElements.showAddonPanel` constant
- **`shortcuts.ts`**: `togglePanel` shortcut handler checks if focus was within the panel before moving it; uses `{ poll: false }` and falls back to `document.body.focus()`
- **`layout.test.ts`**: Added 10 unit tests for `focusOnUIElement` covering all code paths (no elementId, immediate focus, select options, poll/no-poll, polling success/timeout)

#### Manual testing

**Prerequisites:** Run `yarn storybook:ui` and open the Storybook UI in a browser.

**Test 1 – Close addon panel via close button, focus moves to toolbar button**
1. Open the Storybook UI with the addon panel visible (default state).
5. Using the keyboard (Tab), navigate to the "Hide addon panel" close button (✕) in the addon panel header.
6. Press Enter or Space to close the addon panel.
7. Verify that focus moves to the "Show addon panel" button in the toolbar.
8. Press Tab and verify that keyboard navigation continues normally from the toolbar.

**Test 2 – Close addon panel via keyboard shortcut while focus is in the panel**
1. Open the Storybook UI with the addon panel visible.
2. Using the keyboard, navigate to any element inside the addon panel (e.g. an addon tab, the close button, the position toggle button).
3. Press the keyboard shortcut to toggle the panel (default: `A`).
4. Verify that focus moves to the "Show addon panel" button in the toolbar.
5. Press Tab and verify that keyboard navigation continues normally.

**Test 3 – Toggle panel via keyboard shortcut while focus is outside the panel**
1. Open the Storybook UI with the addon panel visible.
2. Click on the sidebar (or any element outside the addon panel) to place focus there.
3. Press the keyboard shortcut to toggle the panel (`A`).
4. Verify that focus does **not** move — it stays wherever it was before (e.g. in the sidebar).
5. Press Tab and verify that keyboard navigation continues normally from the current focus position.

**Test 4 – Re-open addon panel after closing**
1. Close the addon panel using any method (close button or shortcut).
2. Verify the "Show addon panel" button appears in the toolbar.
3. Click or activate the "Show addon panel" button.
4. Verify the addon panel re-opens and functions normally.
5. Verify keyboard navigation works correctly with the panel re-opened.

**Test 5 – Toggle panel shortcut when panel is already hidden**
1. Close the addon panel so it is hidden.
2. Press the keyboard shortcut (`A`) to toggle the panel.
3. Verify the panel opens and focus is not unexpectedly moved.
4. Press Tab and verify keyboard navigation works normally.

**Test 6 – Existing search shortcut still works**
1. Press the search shortcut (default: `/`) to focus the search field.
2. Verify that the search field receives focus and the `select` behavior works (text is selected).
3. Press Escape to close search, then press `/` again — verify polling still works for the search field focus.

comments.body:
Add an option to that function to make the polling behaviour optional. Leave it on by default, but for our new use case, don't poll.

The function should return a boolean to indicate whether focus succeeded. You may make the function async if it results in cleaner code. Add unit tests to cover all relevant use cases for that function.
comments.label_reasoning: The comment requests modifying the function signature to add an optional polling parameter and a boolean return type — a change to the function's contract and consistency across call sites.

comments.author: copilot-swe-agent
comments.body: Added a `poll` option (defaults to `true` for backwards compat) and the function now returns `boolean` synchronously when `poll: false` or when focus succeeds immediately, and `Promise<boolean>` when polling. The second parameter also accepts the old `boolean` form for backwards compatibility with existing callers that pass `select`. Added 10 unit tests covering all code paths. See 787a74c.

review_threads.actionability_reasoning: Requests specific code changes: add an option to make polling optional, make the function return a boolean, optionally make it async, and add unit tests.

comments.author: Sidnioulz
comments.body:
## Problem 1

I want you to account for two use cases:
* The panel is closed by pressing the close button
* The panel is closed by keyboard shortcut _and focus was currently within the panel_

When focus was in a completely different part of the app (e.g. the toolbar, sidebar, preview), we never want to move focus. We only want to move focus when closing the addon panel would result in unpredictable behaviour.


----
## Problem 2
Use the boolean returned by focusOnUIElement to see if we managed to focus `showAddonPanel`. If we failed to focus on it, focus at the start of the document (no need to check if that one worked).
comments.label_reasoning: The comment identifies two incorrect logic paths: focus is moved even when it shouldn't be (wrong condition for when focus was outside the panel), and the boolean return value of focusOnUIElement is not being used to drive the fallback focus behavior.

comments.author: copilot-swe-agent
comments.body:
Addressed both problems:

**Problem 1**: Now checks if `document.activeElement` is inside the panel element (`storybook-panel-root`) before the toggle. Focus is only moved when it was within the panel.

**Problem 2**: Uses `{ poll: false }` and checks the boolean return. Falls back to `document.body.focus()` if `showAddonPanel` button isn't available.

See 787a74c.

review_threads.actionability_reasoning: Requests two specific behavioral changes: only move focus when the panel close would cause unpredictable behavior (not when focus is elsewhere), and use the boolean return value to fall back to document start if focus on showAddonPanel fails.

comments.author: coderabbitai
comments.body:
_⚠️ Potential issue_ | _🟠 Major_

**Fallback can be skipped because this call may return a Promise.**

At Line 35, `focusOnUIElement` defaults to polling and may return `Promise<boolean>`. The `result === false` check only handles the synchronous branch, so fallback focus to `document.body` may never run.



<details>
<summary>Suggested fix</summary>

```diff
-          const result = api.focusOnUIElement(focusableUIElements.showAddonPanel);
+          const result = api.focusOnUIElement(focusableUIElements.showAddonPanel, {
+            poll: false,
+          });
           if (result === false) {
             document.body.focus();
           }
```
</details>

comments.label_reasoning: The `result === false` check only handles the synchronous return path; when `focusOnUIElement` returns a `Promise<boolean>`, the comparison always evaluates to false (a Promise is not === false), so the fallback `document.body.focus()` is never triggered — a clear logic error.
